<br>

Hi! I’m Ben. Or Beni, Benjamin, Benji... I respond to most variations. Welcome to my virtual world. I’m very broadly interested, but the two things that have shaped my own life most consistently and sustainably are music and meditation. Both have also helped me understand a tiny bit better how our minds work (another interest of mine).

I teach meditation and mindfulness, including [MBSR courses in Bern](MBSRCourse.qmd). And I’ve passionately played the piano since childhood—most intensively composing, but also classical music and jazz improvisation. Stay tuned for [upcoming concerts](music.qmd).

Other topics I care about are neuroscience, states of consciousness, and animal welfare, particularly improving the welfare of animals used in research. I worked in animal research myself for many years, doing experiments with mice, rats, monkeys; and some of them severe! I saw how much these animals suffered, contrasting with the relatively little benefit that many animal experiments ultimately bring. Check out this [paper](https://journals.plos.org/plosbiology/article?id=10.1371/journal.pbio.3002667). I think some animal research is still necessary these days, unfortunately. But I am also increasingly infuriated by how much animal suffering and research waste we continue to accept for so little gain. We can, and must, do MUCH better: fewer unnecessary experiments, less harm, better research, and ultimately more benefit from every animal used. Read more [here](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12967-026-08259-y). I hope for a world in which coming generations eventually make animal fully experiments unnecessary.

I’m a professor of medical data science and brain research at the University of Bern, where my group tries to understand how we can make animal research better while reducing the harm we do to animals. Read more about the [STRIDE-Lab](https://ineichen-group.github.io/website/) and the [DCR Medical Data Science Group](https://dcr.unibe.ch/about_us/team/medical_data_science_unit/index_eng.html). Originally, I am a medical doctor but it didn’t take me long to figure out that my heart beats for research.

My own research these days is purely vegetarian: we use existing data and computational models. No animals required.
